name: Rathawi
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: No grammar/phonology of Rathawi located; Glottolog shows only classification/ethnographic sources (Mann 1996; Varkey & Vunnamatla 2018)

sources.citation: Thompson, Charles S. 1895. Rudiments of the Bhili Language. Ahmedabad: United Printing Press.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 3254.104)
sources.note: Predecessor Jungblut worked from (per Koppers 1948); describes Mahikantha/Kherwara Bhili (bhb), not rtw, so only a proxy. Already held by the project at

sources.citation: Varkey, Vinod Wilson & Kishore Kumar Vunnamatla. 2018. A Sociolinguistic Study of Bareli/Pauri and Related Languages. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2018-011. Dallas: SIL International. 197 pp. (includes 'Rathawi' wordlist from Mankodi, Kawant, Baroda dist., Gujarat, from Maggard et al. 1998)
sources.note: Nothing. Lexical similarity/RTT/SRT survey; Rathawi-Mankodi wordlist 80% similar to Bhilali of the Gujarat border; wordlists 'are field transcriptions and have not undergone thorough phonological and grammatical analysis' (p. 74); only 'accent' hits are RPE proficiency descriptors. Cites Maggard, Varkey & Vunnamatla 1998 'The Bhil country of India' (Ms.) and Mathew 1995 'Dungra Bhili survey report' (Ms.).

sources.citation: Tadvi, Revaben Shankarbhai & Shankarbhai Somabhai Tadvi (eds.). 1983. Rāṭhvī Gujarātī Śabdāvalī [Rathwi-Gujarati wordlist]. Ahmedabad: Adivasi Sanshodhan ane Talim Kendra, Gujarat Vidyapith. 47 pp. (Gujarati; for Chhota Udepur Rathwa)
sources.note: Nothing. One-page preface says the glossary is for tribal-area staff and teachers of Chhota Udepur, 'not for linguists'; the rest is a two-column Rathwi-Gujarati wordlist with no pronunciation or accent notes.

sources.citation: Koppers, Wilhelm. 1948. Die Bhil in Zentralindien. Horn/Wien: Ferdinand Berger. (Wiener Beiträge zur Kulturgeschichte und Linguistik 7)
sources.note: Nothing. Ethnography; 'Das sprachliche Problem (Bhili und Gujarati)' p. 21ff and pp. ~22, 30 only report that Thompson 1895 and Jungblut 1938 are the two Bhili grammars and that Bhili is a Gujarati dialect; no accent statement.

sources.citation: Wichelmann, P. H. 1939. Review of L. Jungblut, A Short Bhili Grammar of Jhabua State and adjoining territories (92 pp., Mhow 1938). Anthropos 34: 471.
sources.note: Nothing. Short notice: only predecessor is Thompson 1895; Jungblut gives 'das Gerippe und der Aufbau der Bhil-Sprache' briefly and clearly, intended for Hindi-knowing new missionaries. No content on phonology or accent.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.) 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Part III: The Bhil languages. Calcutta. Section 'Bhili of Jhabua', p. 49, + specimen No. 12 (Jhabua State, Bhopawar Agency). [Glottolog ref 309620, mapped 'Bhili of Jhabua = Rathawi [rtw]']
sources.note: Nothing. Half-page note: final a lengthened to u, palatals pronounced s/z, masc. for neuter, fem. plural -iye, pronouns hamu/tamu, present with se, future of marvu, form kar'telo; no accent or stress remark (the whole volume has no accent statement for any Bhil dialect).

sources.citation: Parakh, Mona. 2019. Preliminary Phonological Description of Rathvi. Language in India 19(4) (April 2019): 266-275. ISSN 1930-2940.

tone.quote: The vowels show contrast in the tongue position, the tongue height and the rounding of the lips. Based on a cursory observation it appears that vowels in Rathvi get relatively longer when they occur in stressed syllables. However, length of vowels and the stress pattern of Rathvi have not been dealt within this work.
tone.locator: p. 272, section 6.1 'The Inventory of Distinctive Vowel Segments' (scope statement also p. 267 sec. 3: 'a preliminary study of the segmental phonology of Rathvi')

sources.citation: Devy, G. N. & Kanji Patel (eds.). c. 2013-2016. Gujarat-ni Bhashao / The Languages of Gujarat (People's Linguistic Survey of India, Gujarat volume). Vadodara: Bhasha Research & Publication Centre / Orient BlackSwan. Chapter on Rathvi.

sources.note: PLSI state volumes give a community-written sketch per language; the Rathwa are the core community of Bhasha's Tejgadh (Chhota Udepur) academy, so a Rathvi chapter is near-certain; PLSI sketches rarely but sometimes note accent.
